notes: The manual shows three diagrams; only the last two images were supplied. I modelled the breadboard version with two four-leg buttons on a common ground rail (the '2x4-pin-button' diagram), which also covers the single four-leg button wiring (GPIO17 input).
The two-leg flying-wire variant (button wired directly to GPIO17 and GND with two wires) is not modelled separately. No two-leg button exists in the catalogue.
The text says GPIO17 is the input pin. The multi-button diagram uses GP5 for the second button.

Each button straddles the centre gap of the breadboard. Row 5 (button 1) and row 10 (button 2) connect to the ground rail. Row 7 connects to GPIO17 and row 12 to GPIO5. Pressing a button joins the ground side to the GPIO side. No external resistor is drawn, so the Pi's internal pull-up must be used.

The breadboard's rows 1-19 are mapped to catalogue columns (e.g. row 5 columns a-e = '5t.a'..'5t.e', columns f-j = '5b.f'..'5b.j'). The left-hand blue (-) rail is 'tn'. The exact rail hole numbers (tn.1, tn.5, tn.10) are approximate and any hole on the rail is equivalent.
The black wire goes to the GND pin next to GP3 (physical pin 6). The catalogue does not say which of GND.1-GND.8 that is, so I used GND.1; all GND pins are symmetric.
